knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=4 t + \sin {t},\,y=t + \cos {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{3 \pi}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=\cos {t} + 4,\,y'(t)=1 - \sin {t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(1 - \sin {t}\right)}{\left(\cos {t} + 4\right)} \\  & =\frac{1 - \sin {t}}{\cos {t} + 4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{3 \pi}{2},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{1 - \sin {\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)}}{\cos {\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)} + 4} \\  & =\frac{1 - \left(-1\right)}{\left(0\right) + 4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

recipes.\\frac{7}{31} - \\frac{3 \\sqrt{2}}{31}: evaluate at half the specified parameter

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=5 t^{2},\,y=t^{5} + t^{3},\,0\le t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=10 t,\,y'(t)=t^{2} \left(5 t^{2} + 3\right).
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(t^{2} \left(5 t^{2} + 3\right)\right)}{\left(10 t\right)} \\  & =\frac{t \left(5 t^{2} + 3\right)}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=1,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(1\right) \left(5 \left(1\right)^{2} + 3\right)}{10} \\  & =\frac{8}{10} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

recipes.\\frac{2}{5}: use y/x instead of derivative ratio

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=2 \sin {2 t},\,y=6 \sin^{2} {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{7 \pi}{12}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=4 \cos {2 t},\,y'(t)=12 \sin {t} \cos {t}=6 \sin {2 t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(6 \sin {2 t}\right)}{\left(4 \cos {2 t}\right)} \\  & =\frac{3 \tan {2 t}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{7 \pi}{12},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{3 \tan {2 \left(\frac{7 \pi}{12}\right)}}{2} \\  & =\frac{3 \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

recipes.-3 - \\frac{3 \\sqrt{3}}{2}: use y/x instead of derivative ratio

$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

x'(t)=5 \cos {t},\,y'(t)=\frac{10 t}{\pi}.

So we have

$$

$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=4 \sin {2 t},\,y=3 \cos^{2} {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi}{12}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=8 \cos {2 t},\,y'(t)=- 6 \sin {t} \cos {t}=- 3 \sin {2 t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- 3 \sin {2 t}\right)}{\left(8 \cos {2 t}\right)} \\  & =- \frac{3 \tan {2 t}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{\pi}{12},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{3 \tan {2 \left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right)}}{8} \\  & =- \frac{3 \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)}{8} \\  & =- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

recipes.\\frac{3 \\sqrt{3}}{8} + \\frac{3}{4}: use y/x instead of derivative ratio

question.:question/problem:

$$
x=5 t^{3} + 1,\,y=3 t^{4} + 3 t^{2},\,0\le t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=15 t^{2},\,y'(t)=6 t \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right).
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(6 t \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right)\right)}{\left(15 t^{2}\right)} \\  & =\frac{2 \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right)}{5 t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=1,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{2 \left(2 \left(1\right)^{2} + 1\right)}{5 \left(1\right)} \\  & =\frac{6}{5} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=- \frac{5 e^{\frac{5}{t}}}{t^{2}},\,y'(t)=- \frac{4 t}{\left(t^{2} + 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.
$$

 

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- \frac{4 t}{\left(t^{2} + 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right)}{\left(- \frac{5 e^{\frac{5}{t}}}{t^{2}}\right)} \\  & =\frac{4 t^{3} e^{- \frac{5}{t}}}{5 \left(t^{2} + 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=4,$ the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{dy}{dx}\,{|}_{t=4} & =\frac{4 \left(4\right)^{3} e^{- \frac{5}{\left(4\right)}}}{5 \left(\left(4\right)^{2} + 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}} \\  & =\frac{256}{95 \sqrt{19} e^{\frac{5}{4}}} \\  & =\frac{256 \sqrt{19}}{1805 e^{\frac{5}{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
